Hey Peter / Sofia — thanks for confirming. Quick responses and next steps:

1) Runway math at current burn: 500,000 tokens / 120,000 tokens/day ≈ 4.1 days. You’re right — that doesn’t reach the 10 business days target.

2) Quick wins to reduce burn (short list):
   - Prompt tuning: remove redundant system messages and reduce max tokens for non-critical assistant responses.
   - Response truncation + post-processing: only return first N tokens for intermediate QA checks, store full output server-side if needed.
   - Local caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (we can enable an automatic cache for the top 50 queries).
   - Batching for high-throughput test flows: enabling batching can reduce per-token overhead when you run parallel test jobs.

If you apply the above we typically see 30–60% reduction in pilot burn depending on prompt complexity; for planning assume a conservative 40% reduction => ~72k tokens/day from current 120k, which would extend runway to ~7 days on the 500k.

3) Committed pricing math (example):
   - On-demand (pilot profile): ~$600 / 1M tokens.
   - Committed: 1M tokens/month at $550 / 1M => $550/month. Effective per-day cost is much lower and predictable for procurement.
   - If you commit to 3–5M/month we can push that to ~$450 / 1M depending on latency SLO and reserved capacity.

4) Recommended move for immediate stability: a) implement 1–2 quick wins (prompt trimming + caching) with engineering, b) accept the 500k credit we just pushed, c) I’ll follow up with a short committed offer for procurement (1M/month at $550 / 1M) that includes a 60-day trial discount if you sign within the next 14 days.

I’ve re-attached the pilot_metrics snapshot and the trial credit agreement for your records. Let me know if you want a quick 20-min session this week to walk through the prompt tuning steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
